messages:
Priya K: Quick check — hitting a weird combo of issues with the Python SDK. Using streaming for rerank responses while paginating embeddings, and occasionally we get a embeddings shape error mid-stream: 
```
ERROR: embedding dims mismatch: expected 1536, got 768
```
Happens only when the page cursor is used + server-side cursor rollups. Any known interactions with auth refresh / retries that could cause truncated payloads?

Alex M: I've seen similar when an auth refresh triggers a reconnect during an active stream. If the client doesn't reattach to the same stream/sequence the server may send a partial page response and the client tries to decode it as a full embedding. Do you have auto_refresh enabled for the token?

Priya K: Not explicitly — we're passing a long-lived bearer token fetched at startup and relying on the SDK to refresh. Using default client.Session(stream=True).

Alex M: Two quick things to try: 1) turn off auto reconnect and do explicit token refresh outside the streaming context, or 2) ensure the SDK replays the last-ok byte-range on reconnect. Also check headers: if the refresh results in a 401 + retry, the streaming connection might be cut and a following paged response could be from a different cursor.

Javier: Another angle — when batching rerank requests we use pad_to_multiple_of=8 for quantized flows. If some pages are padded and some aren't, downstream concat might produce a 768 vector for half the batch. Verify your pad/stack logic.

Priya K: Good call. We're using a helper that stacks pages like: 
```python
# naive stack
def stack_pages(pages):
    return np.vstack(pages)
```
No pad there. Could that explain the 768?

Alex M: Yes. Example: model embedding_dim = 1536, but if you accidentally send a 768-dim model (eg a distilled variant) in some requests, you'll get mixed shapes. Also check the model parameter per page — pagination code sometimes omits the model override when falling back.

Priya K: Hmm — we do have a fallback to a cheaper embed model for older orgs. I didn't think the paginator would mix models across pages but that could happen if the routing fallback occurs on a page boundary.

Morgan: fyi I pushed a small change earlier that tweaks the server cursor TTL and will return a 409 when cursor expired instead of streaming partial content. That might reduce silent shape issues but will surface errors to clients. Deploy is in staging (CI: #3812).

Priya K: @Morgan thanks — noted. Do you know the exact CI job? I can watch staging logs.

Morgan: ci-bot: build/3812 -> staging. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/3812 :shipit:

ci-bot: deployment to staging started for build/3812 :start: 

Javier: For an immediate client-side fix, pad pages when stacking and assert dims early: 
```python
def pad_and_stack(pages, target_dim=1536):
    out = []
    for p in pages:
        if p.shape[1] < target_dim:
            pad = np.zeros((p.shape[0], target_dim - p.shape[1]))
            p = np.concatenate([p, pad], axis=1)
        out.append(p)
    stacked = np.vstack(out)
    assert stacked.shape[1] == target_dim, f"bad dims {stacked.shape}"
    return stacked
```
This will make the error deterministic instead of letting a partial stream silently corrupt downstream rerank.

Priya K: Good — will add that. Any advice about retry behavior? We need to keep streaming user-visible latency low. If we just restart the stream on 401 it's visible.

Alex M: If you can, do optimistic in-band token refresh: monitor token TTL and preemptively refresh ~30s before expiry and re-open a new stream, then reconcile cursors. If not possible, add idempotent markers per page (page_id) so server can drop duplicates and client can resume safely.

Priya K: Page ids are already in the paginator. Will add the preemptive refresh + pad-and-stack check. I'll open an issue with the steps.

Javier: One more: enable verbose debug for the HTTP connection to capture any connection resets (`requests`/httpx has event hooks). That helped us find a proxy dropping keepalive.

Priya K: Thanks all. I'll post results here after trying patches. :thumbsup:
